body:
FROM THE P5 HOLLOW-RAIL LENS, 2026-08-19. Some are fixed on the branch; these are what remain, and
each is a rail that would stay green while the behaviour it names is broken.

1. bless-toggle.test.ts asserts criterion 10's second half with `expect(Array.isArray(me.lawFrom([])))
   .toBe(true)`. lawFromImpl iterates `for (const version of versions)`, so lawFrom([]) is [] always
   and Array.isArray([]) is a tautology. "Leaves already-bound law serving" is asserted by NOTHING —
   a pause that retroactively unbound every law on the channel passes. Bind it with a real read
   through the door, not with `def` (registry level).

2. drop-two-sided.test.ts proves SURVIVAL at the bytes and REMOVAL only at the gather. A drop that
   struck the pool declaration and purged nothing satisfies all three assertions. That is T40's shape,
   and the file header, the code comment and criterion 13 all claim the byte level. MemoryBackend
   exposes holds(id) and Gateway accepts a channelBackend factory, so the test can keep a handle per
   pool and assert holds(target) === false / holds(bystander) === true. drop() closes the store, so
   the handle must be captured at open time. Same file: "bob's binding survives" asserts only that
   the pool has some deltas.

3. channel-open.test.ts asserts `arrivalLog()[0]`, which is the GENESIS operator marker, not the
   peer's claim the comment names — Gateway.boot appends genesis first. A channel that crossed
   constitutional deltas and dropped every data delta passes. Hold the delta in a const, as the
   second test already does. Its `primary.length > 0` two-sidedness is decorative — bob's ground
   always holds genesis.

4. friend-scenario.test.ts re-boots with a TEST-AUTHORED channelBackend that re-implements
   channelBackendFor's path mangling. The shipped read path is `loam serve`, which wires that factory
   itself. REMOVING channelBackend FROM cmdServe LEAVES EVERY RAIL GREEN while a real reader gets
   null. The header says "Nothing is stubbed"; the reading process is hand-wired. Drive the CLI.

5. THE SPEC NAMES THREE VERIFICATION FILES THAT DO NOT EXIST — criteria 5, 14 and 15 point at
   bare-alias-explicit / drop-shared-delta / pool-isolation, which were folded into other files.
   Criterion 17 says "verified by npm run check", which any green suite satisfies, so it verifies
   nothing specific. Either restore the filenames or amend the criteria; a criterion naming a file
   that does not exist is worse than one naming none.

6. THE TICKET FREEZES NOTHING: t186's shard carries rails: [] so rails-guard protects none of these
   13 files. Declare them at P3, now that they exist.

7. bind-on-arrival.test.ts's header still describes the PRE-FIX state ("does not yet SERVE", "the
   skipped rail below is the visible hole") and there is no longer any skipped rail in the file. A
   reader is told the serving half is unproven, so nobody would notice if that rail were later
   weakened. Delete the stale paragraph.

ALSO NAMED CLEAN, so it is not re-audited: freeze-toggle, standing-sync (the stop-the-poller half is
a real second side), last-synced (the quiet-vs-unreachable pair pins H9 at the level that matters),
prefix-injective, channel-subscribe, and friend-scenario's value assertions through a real door.
title: Rail defects in the T186 set: a vacuous branch, a tautology, a gather-level purge check, and a hand-wired read path
